newsitem.title: CHINA: Dazhong Taxi to set up 50-mln-yuan call system.
newsitem.headline: Dazhong Taxi to set up 50-mln-yuan call system.

text.p: Shanghai Dazhong Taxi Co plans to set up a taxi calling system using Australian technology and involving investment of 50 million yuan ($6 million), a company official said on Friday.
The system, which provides a fast response taxi telephone booking and dispatch service, has been developed by Australian firm Sigtec.

A Sigtech statement said the first phase of the system incorporates a sophisticated computer control centre for receiving bookings and automatically dispatching them to the taxi closest to the customer.
It is the first such system in China, Sigtec said, adding there was huge potential for further sales in China.
The first phase, worth about A$2 million ($1.56 million), will go into operation later this year, the Dazhong official said. The system is seen completed within three years.
Australian Prime Minister John Howard was to attend a ceremony marking the deal during a trip to Shanghai on Sunday.
Dazhong would take the majority stake of the system of which Shanghai's Bureau of Public Utilities Administration and other taxi companies would also have shares, the official said.
